title: feat(desktop): record the webcam as its own file on the screen's clock (NIW2-571)
body:
PR 1 of the webcam-track stack ([design #437](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/437), Linear [NIW2-571](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-571), parent [NIW2-565](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-565)). Base: `design/niw2-565-webcam-track`.

## What this does

With the camera on, a take now writes the webcam into its own file, `.kaipu/<id>.webcam.mp4`, next to the screen recording. Both files use the same clock, and the sidecar stores the gap between their starts (`webcam.startOffsetMs`) with a quality flag. This is the recording half of the design only: the editor does not use the file yet, and the camera bubble is **still burned into the screen** on purpose. It leaves the capture in the last PR of the stack, so `main` never records a take with no face anywhere.

## Why

Auto-zoom crops the face out because the bubble exists only as screen pixels. Every later PR in the stack (editor layer, export, Share) needs a webcam file that lines up with the screen to within a frame. This PR produces it.

## What changes for you

- **Camera-on takes record a second file**, H.264 with no audio: 1280×720 @ 30 fps, or 1080 lines while framing is active. It costs about 19 MB/min of disk and a second hardware encoder. Nothing shows it in the UI yet.
- **The bubble preview asks the camera for 16:9 at 720 lines or more** (it was 4:3 at 480). Chromium shares one capture per device, so a smaller preview would have capped the webcam file. On cameras that make 16:9 by cropping a 4:3 sensor (the MacBook camera), the face in the bubble looks slightly closer. The preview also costs a bit more CPU whenever the camera is on.
- **Deleting a recording also deletes its webcam file.**
- A webcam that fails, hangs (3 s deadline) or is unplugged never fails the take; the take continues with the screen only.

## What to review

1. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:773` — stop order.** Decide whether finalizing the webcam after the screen and before the tracks stop can race an abort, or hold the camera light on. Note the waits, both bounded: up to 3 s for the webcam's first timestamp, and 3 s to open the camera (`:228`).
2. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/webcam-track.ts:80` — `webcamStartOffset`.** The sign (`webcamT0 − screenT0`, both on the renderer clock) and the "exact" vs "estimated" rule. Every later PR builds on this number.
3. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/recording-writer.ts:197` and `:372` — two sessions per take.** A failed webcam write must never fail the take; a failed screen write discards the webcam; salvage moves both.
4. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/recording-hub.ts:371` — the new IPC `kind`.** It comes from the renderer. `recordingWriterKind` maps anything unknown to `"screen"`, so it cannot steer a path. Check you agree.
5. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts:351` — reacquiring after the camera is turned off and on during the countdown** (Codex finding C1).

**Safe to skim:** `shared/types/*` and `preload/index.ts` (type plumbing for `kind`), `scripts/webcam-track-check.ts` and its report module (a dev tool), the docs pages, and the test files.

## Proof

| Pause/resume/stop act on both; a failing webcam never fails the take | Same-call pause/resume; open deadline; encoder/write failures isolated | Engine tests "pauses and resumes…", "a camera that never answers…", hub "a failed webcam write never stops the take" | Unit tests pass |

## Decisions

- **Bubble protection is not in this PR.** Options: protect the bubble now, or last. Taken: last (NIW2-576). Until the editor composes the webcam, a protected bubble would leave takes with no face anywhere.
- **The bubble preview asks for 16:9 at 720 lines or more.** Options: keep 4:3/480 and accept a smaller webcam file, open the camera once and share the stream between windows, or raise the preview. Taken: raise the preview, the smallest change. Cost: a slightly closer field of view on cropping cameras, and more CPU for the preview.
- **Webcam size comes from the first encoded frame**, not `getSettings()`, because the shared capture can deliver a size other than the one requested.
- **The camera gets 3 s to open** (`WEBCAM_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS`). That fits inside the store's 10 s start timeout and leaves time for the screen probe and the encoder.
- **Turning the camera off mid-take ends the file and releases the camera; turning it back on mid-take records nothing more.** That is the spec's open question 7, left for later.
- **A recovered stranded pair gets no `webcam` sidecar field**, because its offset was never written and the code does not invent one. The file stays paired by id, so delete removes it.
- **`recordedLayout` is the bubble's shape, size, mirror and framing, without its on-screen position**, because the renderer does not know where the bubble is. The editor-seeding PR (NIW2-573) needs main to add the position, or falls back to the default corner.

Rounds: 4 with Opus 5.5 (fresh-context reviewer) and 2 with Codex (cross-provider, read-only). The high-risk budget is 5; the 6th was a narrow Codex check of C1 and C2 only.
**Verdict for 9ab51d97 (patch-id ea2966a25cd7): approved, only nits remain.** Opus re-checked 9ab51d97 (the agent-review fixes); Codex verified C1/C2 (2ec5de75, 1486d87f).

Follow-ups (nits):
- S3: re-read the exact first timestamp after stop when the 3 s wait returned "estimated".
- S4: document the ±1 frame per pause bound, and the case of a pause before the webcam's first frame.
- S5: `strand()` should discard a failed webcam session, or one without metadata.
- S6: salvage should not overwrite an existing `<name>.webcam.mp4`.
- S8: if the screen finalize throws in `stop()`, the camera light stays on (a pre-existing pattern).
- S9: `endWebcam` should not `close()` a failed source.

## Checks

- `cd apps/kaipu-record && vitest run`: exit 0, 311 files, 3026 tests passed (on 1486d87f).
- Pre-push `verify:local` (lint, oxfmt, build, check-types): passed on push. Lint reports 0 errors and 18 warnings that were already there, none in touched files.

## Manual verification

This is owner QA; agents do not run Electron on the owner's machine.

**Setup:** `git fetch && git checkout feature/niw2-571-webcam-recorder && bun install && bun run dev` (desktop app). The vault is the dev one (`kaipu-record-dev`).

**1. A take writes both files**
- Turn the camera on and record 10 s of the display.
- `ls "<vault>/.kaipu/"`
- Expect: `<id>.webcam.mp4` next to the recording. QuickTime plays it: your face, not mirrored, about 1280×720.
- Broken if: there is no webcam file, it is under 720 lines, or it is mirrored.

**2. The check script**
- `cd apps/kaipu-record && bun run webcam-track:check <id>`
- Expect: both durations, `start offset: <n> ms quality: exact`, the size 1280x720 @ 30 fps, and `OK`.
- Broken if: `estimated`, a size under 720 lines, or `✗`.

**3. Clap test, with a pause**
- Record, clap in front of the camera, pause for 5 s, resume, clap again, stop.
- In the two files, the claps should be within one frame (about 33 ms) once the offset is applied.
- Broken if: the second clap drifts by more than a frame.

**4. A broken camera does not break the take**
- Pick a camera another app is holding, or unplug the camera mid-take.
- Expect: the take still saves with the screen only.

**5. Delete**
- Delete the recording in the library.
- Expect: both files are gone.

## What I did not verify

- Any real take: the file's size, the `exact` quality from mediabunny's private field across two outputs, the clap alignment, and whether Chromium serves 1280×720 to the recorder while the bubble holds the camera.
- Windows.
- The extra CPU from the second encoder plus the 720-line preview.
